text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski may meet Hungarian President Arpad Goncz on August 24.
- The doctoral theses of Prime Minister Gyula Horn and opposition Smallholder Jozsef Torgyan should be made available to all, data protection ombudsman Laszlo Majtenyi said.
- Agnes Cser may be reomved from her post as head of the Health INsurance Fund.
- The Defense Ministry plans no major cuts in its 1998 budget.
- Christian Democrat President Gyorgy Giczy said he has little hope ahead of today's reconciliatory talks with the party's Vice-President Zsolt Semjen.
- Formula 1 weekend starts today with free practice.
NEPSZABADSAG
- An Interior Ministry draft proposes the establishment of tolerance zones for prostitutes.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Finance Ministry plans to write off 59 billion forints debt owed to the budget mainly by the social security systems.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS
- Milling wheat futures for May 1998 have reached 30,000 forints per tonne.
- The number of foreigners' guest nights dropped 1.4 percent in the January-June period year-on-year while domestic tourists spent on average 5.6 percent omre nights in hotels.
- Commerzbank's first half profits rose 43 percent over the same period of 1996.
- Konzumbank first half profits rose to 121 million forints from 29 million in the first half of 1996.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Food retailer Julius Meinl reported first half profits 9 percent below the same period of 1996.
